Buyers returned for a second straight session after Unity Software announced early engine support for Meta's upcoming VR headset, but the rally hinges on something that has not happened yet and may not for months.

The buying has continued for a second day, it seems. It’s turning Unity Software (NYSE:U | U Price Prediction) into a live test of what early engine support for a new virtual-reality headset is worth. Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) is the maker of that device, Meta VR Glasses, which is expected to reach retail customers next spring.
Unity Software stock is up 5% to $43.02 in Thursday afternoon trading, marking a second straight advance for the shares.
Checking in on the peers, Roblox (NYSE:RBLX) shares are inching up 0.8% to $42.70. Meanwhile, Take-Two Interactive (NASDAQ:TTWO) stock is falling 3% to $201.94.
At the same time, the VanEck Video Gaming and eSports ETF (NASDAQ:ESPO) is up 0.3% to $96.79. For a broad-market check, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is down 0.2% to $761.05. Unity Software stock is trading as a single-name story inside a gaming group that’s barely moving and a broad market that’s falling.
Day-One Engine Support for a New Headset Keeps Buyers Engaged
Unity Software announced day-one engine support for Meta VR Glasses in the previous session, noting that developers can begin building and testing experiences now, which gives studios more time to prepare titles before the hardware reaches retail customers. No new company release has been confirmed in the current session.
Timing anchors the bull case for Unity Software. Engine support that lands well before the hardware puts the company in front of every studio planning a title for Meta VR Glasses, and developers generally reuse the tools they already know. Unity Software held its August earnings call. On it, chief executive Matt Bromberg stated, “We are really excited to be in a position to help platforms, any and all platforms, be optimized for Unity, because Unity is by far the leading platform for game making in the world.”
However, Unity Software’s revenue from Meta VR Glasses depends on developer adoption that hasn’t happened yet. Unity Software stock is down 3% year to date, leaving the shares below where they began the year despite the rally.
Advertising drives Unity Software’s growth for now. In Q2 2026, Unity Software’s revenue rose 23.9% year over year to $546.47 million, led by a 35% jump in Grow Solutions to $389 million on the strength of Unity Vector AI in the Unity Ads Network. Those results give Unity Software the financial room to fund a virtual-reality push while headset demand takes shape.
The slide in Take-Two shares and the small gain in Roblox stock leave the rest of the gaming group out of step with Unity Software. Roblox and Take-Two carried heavier weightings than Unity Software in the VanEck fund as of June 30, at 7% and 6.9% of net assets against 4.7%, which helps explain the ETF’s modest move. Nintendo (OTC:NTDOY) is another holding.
Developer Adoption Decides What Unity Software’s Head Start Is Worth
Unity Software’s next major checkpoint is its Q3 2026 report, with the company guiding its strategic revenue to $540 million to $550 million and targeting a profit under standard accounting rules in the quarter. Shareholders can watch for signs of studios committing titles to Meta VR Glasses before the device reaches retail customers next spring. Named launch titles from well-known studios could give the shares fresh support, while a quiet stretch may leave the rally vulnerable.
Repeat buying of the same announcement can lose momentum quickly, particularly for Unity Software stock given its history of sharp swings, as the return from Unity’s Meta VR Glasses support depends on studios shipping titles for a device that isn’t on sale yet.

pages.text:
Take-Two Interactive Drops Major GTA 6 Online & PC Release Updates
We are just one month away from the highly anticipated November release of Grand Theft Auto (GTA) 6. Rockstar Games has spent months showcasing its next-generation open world. Now, Take-Two Interactive has stepped in and recently released a new official statement. This statement clarifies the future of GTA 6 Online, the PC release strategy, and the current iteration of GTA Online.
GTA 6 will launch this November strictly as a single-player title. Therefore, players will initially focus entirely on the core narrative. The story centers around dual protagonists, Jason and Lucia. Furthermore, they will explore a returning Vice City and a massively expanded state of Leonida. Rockstar designed this map to be massive. In fact, it scales well beyond the vast size of Red Dead Redemption 2.
However, the developers did not just focus on raw map size. Instead, they built the world around dense detailing. Players will encounter highly complex NPCs, diverse activities, and deep interactions. According to Take-Two, this dynamic single-player experience forms the true heart and soul of the game.
The Future of GTA Online & GTA 6 Multiplayer
Take-Two is deliberately separating the single-player launch from its online business. Currently, Rockstar has not officially revealed a release date, launch window, or name for a GTA 6 multiplayer mode.
Meanwhile, the existing version of GTA Online is not going anywhere. Take-Two explicitly confirmed that they will continue supporting the current GTA Online after GTA 6 releases and beyond. The current multiplayer version remains incredibly lucrative. As a result, the company will maintain active support for it.
Still, some details about Rockstar’s unreleased multiplayer work have surfaced. Recently, legal filings from a company employment dispute referenced a highly confidential “online 32-player format”. The filing does not explicitly name GTA 6 Online. Moreover, it remains unconfirmed if 32 players will serve as the final lobby cap. Nevertheless, it stands as the clearest public reference to Rockstar’s upcoming multiplayer framework.
What About the GTA 6 PC Release?
Currently, Rockstar has not announced an official PC version for GTA 6. However, Take-Two addressed the platform directly in their recent statement. The company’s general strategy is to launch games on any platform that holds a “meaningful audience” over time.
Furthermore, Take-Two emphasized a shifting focus within the company. They explicitly stated that the PC platform is becoming increasingly important to their overall operations. Therefore, while a PC port remains shrouded in mystery for now, a future release seems inevitable as long as the platform remains viable.
We will have to wait and see what Rockstar Games does when it comes to GTA 6 Online and a PC release. Until then, we will keep you updated on all future GTA 6 developments. Stay tuned to TechJuice for timely updates.

GameStop (NYSE:GME | GME Price Prediction) stock popped 4% to $24.79 on Wednesday, extending recent gains driven by Chairman and CEO Ryan Cohen’s continued open-market share purchases. Take-Two Interactive Software (NASDAQ:TTWO) shares advanced 3% to $209.78, while Roblox (NYSE:RBLX) stock also rose 3% to $42.53. Gaming-related names found support as attention remained focused on insider buying at GameStop.
The VanEck Video Gaming and eSports ETF (NASDAQ:ESPO) climbed 1% to $96.84. Broader markets moved higher, with the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE ARCA:SPY) up 0.52% to $768.20. GameStop’s latest headlines center on Ryan Cohen’s repeated buying, which has reinforced investor focus. The company recently reported a mixed quarter in which sales declined 19% while net income rose 77%, aided by cost cuts, collectibles growth, and investment gains, including from its eBay stake.
Ryan Cohen purchased 450,000 GameStop shares at approximately $23.48 each, for a total value of about $10.6 million, according to a recent SEC filing. The transaction follows earlier September purchases that included roughly 1.15 million shares for about $26.4 million and 1 million shares for about $20.4 million. Cohen’s direct holdings now stand near 41 million shares, representing roughly 8.8% of the company when including warrants.
These open-market buys form part of a broader pattern of insider accumulation throughout the year with no reported sales. The activity has helped sustain attention on GameStop shares even as the traditional video-game hardware and software business faces ongoing pressure.
Take-Two Interactive and Roblox Also Advance
Take-Two Interactive stock posted a solid gain. The company develops and publishes major interactive entertainment titles across console, PC, and mobile platforms. Take-Two Interactive shares have responded to both sector sentiment and its own pipeline developments in recent sessions.
Roblox stock moved higher as well. Roblox operates a platform that allows users to create and share immersive experiences, generating revenue primarily through in-platform purchases. Both Take-Two Interactive and Roblox operate in the broader gaming ecosystem but differ from GameStop’s retail and collectibles-focused model.
The VanEck Video Gaming and eSports ETF’s advance reflected measured strength across the niche. GameStop’s second-quarter results showed net sales of $790.2 million, down 19% year over year, while net income rose 77% to $298.7 million. Collectibles sales grew sharply and now account for a larger share of the mix, helped by cost discipline and non-operating gains tied to the company’s investment portfolio.
Similarities among GameStop, Take-Two Interactive, and Roblox include exposure to consumer spending on entertainment and digital content. Differences appear in business models, with GameStop emphasizing physical retail, collectibles, and balance-sheet management, while the other two focus on content creation and platform engagement. Insider conviction and a larger cash and investment position remain central to the GameStop narrative.
Ryan Cohen’s repeated purchases have provided a clear catalyst for GameStop stock in recent weeks. The mixed quarterly results highlight progress on profitability and mix shift even as top-line challenges persist. Strategic interest around the eBay investment and ongoing cost management continue to factor into investor discussions.
Investors should consider keeping position sizes modest given the elevated volatility that has long characterized GameStop stock. Further insider buying, sustained collectibles momentum, or clearer progress on strategic initiatives could support the shares, while weaker sales trends or shifts in retail sentiment may renew pressure across the group.

Take Two Interactive Software (TTWO) Stock Looks Close To Fair Value
Wed, September 30, 2026 at 8:09 AM PDT 3 min read
Take-Two Interactive Software shares have had a mixed few years, with a strong multi year gain sitting alongside more recent weakness, and that raises a clear question for you as an investor: Is the current US$202.78 price properly grounded in the cash the business is expected to generate, or has the share price moved out of step with those cash flows?

Jefferies just put a target on Roblox that sits well below where shares are trading, and the rest of the gaming group barely flinched. Whether the firm has correctly read Roblox's bookings path will determine if today's selloff is just…
Published September 28, 2026, 9:41am ET · 3 min read

This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
A Jefferies downgrade is landing directly on Roblox (NYSE:RBLX | RBLX Price Prediction) while the rest of the video game group barely budges. Roblox stock is down 6% to $43.72 after Jefferies cut its rating to Underperform. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is down 0.52%, so the overall market is offering only a moderate drag against a selloff concentrated in one gaming name.
Take-Two Interactive (NASDAQ:TTWO) shares are up 0.1% to $201.59, holding steady as the downgrade stays contained to Roblox. Meanwhile, GameStop (NYSE:GME) stock is down 0.7% to $23.23, a modest slip next to the Roblox selloff. Roblox is absorbing the damage alone. Rounding out the picture, the VanEck Video Gaming and eSports ETF (NASDAQ:ESPO) tracks a basket of video game and esports stocks in that corner of the market.
That split between Roblox and its closest peers points to a reassessment of one company’s outlook, with whether Jefferies has read Roblox’s bookings path correctly now the central question.
Jefferies Questions Roblox’s Bookings Outlook
Jefferies downgraded Roblox to Underperform from Hold and set a $38 price target. The firm argued that the rally in Roblox shares following the company’s most recent quarterly results had priced in an overly optimistic outlook for bookings. That critique goes after the metric many Roblox followers lean on most to judge how much spending the platform can generate.
Beyond bookings, Jefferies argued that user and monetization growth in the United States and Canada would recover more slowly and at higher cost than investors currently expect. Weaker recovery economics in those markets would pressure Roblox on two fronts at once, reducing growth while lifting expenses, and that combination explains why the firm views the recent run in Roblox stock as overextended.
Steady trading in Take-Two stock frames the Jefferies note as a verdict on Roblox’s own bookings path. Roblox depends on a user-generated platform and spending inside those experiences, while Take-Two develops and sells its own franchise games. Any monetization worry at Roblox therefore says little about Take-Two’s prospects.
Diversified funds hold Roblox, Take-Two and GameStop side by side. In funds such as the VanEck Video Gaming and eSports ETF, a hit to one holding gets diluted across the basket. That dilution is what a stock-specific downgrade typically looks like when the rest of the group holds its ground. In that structure, Roblox shareholders carry the downgrade’s full cost while fund holders feel a far smaller share.
What decides the debate is whether Roblox engagement holds up against the bookings outlook Jefferies is questioning. That answer stays out of view until Roblox reports its next quarter, so Roblox stock may remain sensitive to analyst commentary in the meantime. A sturdy engagement showing would weaken the downgrade’s logic, while another soft bookings figure would lend the firm’s view real weight.
The sharp move in Roblox stock against a nearly flat gaming group argues for a measured approach. Shareholders should keep their positions moderate while the bookings debate plays out, and anyone adding shares after the decline could build exposure in stages.
Traders should look to Roblox’s next quarterly report, where the company’s bookings and engagement figures will put Jefferies’ thesis to a direct test. Any change in user trends across the United States and Canada could confirm or challenge the slower, costlier recovery the firm described.
